articleTitle: Corrigendum to “A Quiver Construction of Symmetric Crystals”
Breakdown for the Camassa–Holm Equation Using Decay Criteria and Persistence in Weighted Spaces
abstract: We exhibit a sufficient condition in terms of decay at infinity of the initial data for the finite time blowup of strong solutions to the Camassa–Holm equation: a wave breaking will occur as soon as the initial data decay faster at infinity than the solitons. In the case of data decaying slower than solitons we provide persistence results for the solution in weighted L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>-spaces for a large class of moderate weights. Explicit asymptotic profiles illustrate the optimality of these results.

In this paper, we extend the notion of Futaki invariant to big and nef classes in such a way that it defines a continuous function on the Kähler cone up to the boundary. We apply this concept to prove that reduced normal crossing singularities are sufficient to check K-semistability. A similar improvement on Donaldson’s lower bound for the Calabi energy is given.

articleTitle: Energy Minimization, Periodic Sets and Spherical Designs
abstract: We study energy minimization for pair potentials among periodic sets in Euclidean spaces. We derive some sufficient conditions under which a point lattice locally minimizes the energy associated to a large class of potential functions. This allows us, in particular, to prove a local version of Cohn and Kumar’s conjecture that A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf>, and the Leech lattice are globally universally optimal, regarding energy minimization, and among periodic sets of fixed point density.

articleTitle: A Class of Infinite-dimensional Frobenius Manifolds and their Submanifolds
abstract: We construct a class of infinite-dimensional Frobenius manifolds on the space of pairs of certain even functions meromorphic inside or outside the unit circle. Via a bi-Hamiltonian recursion relation, the principal hierarchies associated to such Frobenius manifolds are found to be certain extensions of the dispersionless two-component BKP hierarchy. Moreover, we show that these manifolds contain finite-dimensional Frobenius submanifolds as defined on the orbit space of Coxeter groups of types B and D.

articleTitle: Analytic Extension Techniques for Unitary Representations of Banach–Lie Groups
abstract: Let (G,θ) be a Banach–Lie group with involutive automorphism θ, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta,\ \mathfrak {g=h}\ \oplus\ \mathfrak q$</tex> be the θ-eigenspaces in the Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex> of G, and H=(G<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</sup>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> be the identity component of its group of fixed points. An Olshanski semigroup is a semigroup S⊆G of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S=H\ {\mathrm exp}(W)$</tex>, where W is an open Ad(H)-invariant convex cone in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak q$</tex> and the polar map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H\ \times W\rightarrow S,\ (h,x)\mapsto h\ {\mathrm exp}\ x$</tex> is a diffeomorphism. Any such semigroup carries an involution * satisfying <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(h\ {\mathrm exp}\ x)^*=({\mathrm exp}\ x)h^{-1}$</tex>. Our central result, generalizing the Lüscher–Mack theorem for finite-dimensional groups, asserts that any locally bounded *-representation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi :S\rightarrow B\ (\mathcal H)$</tex> with a dense set of smooth vectors defines by “analytic continuation” a unitary representation of the simply connected Lie group G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> with Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g_c=\mathfrak h\ +\ {\mathrm i}\mathfrak q$</tex>. We also characterize those unitary representations of G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> obtained by this construction. With similar methods, we further show that semibounded unitary representations extend to holomorphic representations of complex Olshanski semigroups.

articleTitle: Some Singular Limit Laminations of Embedded Minimal Planar Domains
abstract: In this paper, we give two examples of sequences of embedded minimal planar domains in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^3$</tex> which converge to singular laminations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^3$</tex>. In contrast with the situation for embedded minimal disks, these examples do not arise from complete embedded minimal planar domains and highlight some of the subtleties inherent in understanding refined properties of embedded minimal planar domains.

articleTitle: Refined Asymptotics for Second Spectral Moment of Rankin–Selberg L-Functions at the Special Points
abstract: We establish a new asymptotic formula with power saving in the remainder for the second spectral moment of the special values of Rankin–Selberg L-functions L(s<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf>,Q⊗u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf>), where Q(z) is a fixed normalized holomorphic newform of even integral weight 2k ≥ 4, prime level p and trivial nebentypus, and {u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf>(z)}<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j≥1</inf> is the orthonormal basis of Hecke–Maass cuspidal eigenforms with the Laplacian eigenvalues <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_j=s_j(1-s_j),\ (s_j=\frac {1}{2}+it_j)$</tex>, for the modular group SL(2,Z). The nonvanishing of these special L-values arises as the dissolving condition in the Phillips–Sarnak's work on deformation of discrete groups and existence of cusp forms.

articleTitle: The First Boundary Value Problem for Abreu’s Equation
abstract: In this paper, we prove the existence and regularity of solutions to the first boundary value problem for Abreu’s equation, which is a fourth-order nonlinear partial differential equation closely related to the Monge–Ampère equation. The first boundary value problem can be formulated as a variational problem for the energy functional. The existence and uniqueness of maximizers can be obtained by the concavity of the functional. The main ingredients of the paper are the a priori estimates and an approximation result, which enable us to prove that the maximizer is smooth in dimension 2.

articleTitle: Rankin–Cohen Brackets for Jacobi Forms and Tensor Products of Discrete Series Representations of the Jacobi Group
abstract: Explicit formulae for Rankin–Cohen brackets for Jacobi forms are obtained by pure Lie theoretic means. The Lie algebraic nature of these holomorphic bi-differential operators, which map pairs of Jacobi forms onto another such form, is unveiled, along with their relationship with the decompositions of tensor products of two (anti-)holomorphic discrete series representations of the Jacobi group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak G$</tex> into direct sums of similar representations. These decompositions, which turn out to be nonmultiplicity-free, are a problem of an independent interest, which is explicitly solved. Some of the obtained brackets are shown to be intertwiners, projecting the appropriate tensor product onto a direct summand. The first mentioned goal is reached by characterizing all the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak G$</tex>-equivariant holomorphic bi-differential operators, through establishing a one-to-one correspondence between them and the null vectors in the tensor products of two Verma <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex>-modules, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex> the complexified Lie algebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak G$</tex>. A large class of pairs of such modules is considered, the remaining situations being relegated to a future work. A thorough analysis of the structure of the tensor products, based on Borho’s isomorphism, which provides a factorization of the universal enveloping algebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex>, yields explicit formulae for the sought after null vectors; they turn out to be completely determined by the null vectors in tensor products of three Verma <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {sl}_2$</tex>-modules. The bi-differential operators associated with the obtained null vectors are then shown to be Rankin–Cohen brackets for Jacobi forms. The Lie theoretic approach developed here supplies a unifying framework within which results of previous investigations undertaken by different authors, using techniques pertaining to the realm of number theory, are recovered, provided with new interpretations and generalized. In particular, Böcherer’s generic dimensions are shown to be given by the above-mentioned multiplicities.

This is to present the newfound q-algebraic relation ℓ(x)ℓ(y)=ℓ((1−x)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>y)ℓ(−x(1−x−y)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>y)ℓ(x(1−y)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>), where x and y are q-commuting variables, yx=qxy, and ℓ is Heine’s q-exponential function, ℓ(z)=1+z/(1−q)+z<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/(1−q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>)(1−q)+⋯ . This relation represents the most direct q-analog of the classical five-term dilogarithm relation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal L(x)+\mathcal L(y)=\mathcal L(y/(1-x))+\mathcal L(-xy/(1-x-y))+\mathcal L(x/(1-y))$</tex> where x and y are ordinary commuting variables, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal L(z)=L(1/(1-1/z))$</tex>, and L is the Rogers dilogarithm.

articleTitle: Grafting Rays Fellow Travel Teichmüller Geodesics
abstract: Given a measured geodesic lamination on a hyperbolic surface, grafting the surface along multiples of the lamination defines a path in Teichmüller space, called the grafting ray. We show that every grafting ray, after reparameterization, is a Teichmüller quasi-geodesic and stays in a bounded neighborhood of some Teichmüller geodesic. As part of our approach, we show that grafting rays have controlled dependence on the starting point; that is, for any measured geodesic lamination λ, the map of Teichmüller space which is defined by grafting along λ is L-Lipschitz with respect to the Teichmüller metric, where L is a universal constant. This Lipschitz property follows from an extension of grafting to an open neighborhood of Teichmüller space in the space of quasi-Fuchsian groups.

articleTitle: Smooth Representations of GLm(D) VI: Semisimple Types
abstract: We give a complete description of the category of smooth complex representations of the multiplicative group of a central simple algebra over a locally compact nonarchimedean local field. More precisely, for each inertial class in the Bernstein spectrum, we construct a type and compute its Hecke algebra. The Hecke algebras that arise are all naturally isomorphic to products of affine Hecke algebras of type A. We also prove that, for cuspidal classes, the simple type is unique up to conjugacy.

articleTitle: Asymptotics of the Instantons of Painlevé I
abstract: The 0-instanton solution of Painlevé I is a sequence (u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n,0</inf>) of complex numbers which appears universally in many enumerative problems in algebraic geometry, graph theory, matrix models, and 2-dimensional quantum gravity. The asymptotics of the 0-instanton (u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n,0</inf>) for large n were obtained by the third author using the Riemann–Hilbert approach. For k=0,1,2,…, the k-instanton solution of Painlevé I is a doubly indexed sequence (u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n,k</inf>) of complex numbers that satisfies an explicit quadratic nonlinear recursion relation. The goal of the paper is three-fold: (a) to compute the asymptotics of the 1-instanton sequence (u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n,1</inf>) to all orders in 1/n by using the Riemann–Hilbert method, (b) to present formulas for the asymptotics of (u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n,k</inf>) for fixed k and to all orders in 1/n using resurgent analysis, and (c) to confirm numerically the predictions of resurgent analysis. We point out that the instanton solutions display a new type of Stokes behavior, induced from the tritronquée Painlevé transcendents, and which we call the induced Stokes phenomenon. The asymptotics of the 2-instanton and beyond exhibits new phenomena not seen in 0 and 1-instantons, and their enumerative context is at present unknown.

Boij–Söderberg theory is the study of two cones: the cone of Betti diagrams of standard graded minimal free resolutions over a polynomial ring and the cone of cohomology tables of coherent sheaves over projective space. We provide a new interpretation of these partial orders in terms of the existence of nonzero homomorphisms, for both the general and equivariant constructions. These results provide new insights into the families of modules and sheaves at the heart of Boij–Söderberg theory: Cohen–Macaulay modules with pure resolutions and supernatural sheaves. In addition, they suggest the naturality of these partial orders and provide tools for extending Boij–Söderberg theory to other graded rings and projective varieties.

articleTitle: Gel’fand–Calderón’s Inverse Problem for Anisotropic Conductivities on Bordered Surfaces in ℝ3
abstract: Let X be a smooth bordered surface in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^3$</tex> with a smooth boundary and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat \sigma$</tex> a smooth anisotropic conductivity on X. If the genus of X is given, then starting from the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda _{\hat \sigma}$</tex> on ∂X, we give an explicit procedure to find a unique Riemann surface Y (up to a biholomorphism), an isotropic conductivity σ on Y and a quasiconformal diffeomorphism F:X→Y which transforms <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat \sigma$</tex> into σ. As a corollary, we obtain the following uniqueness result: if σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> are two smooth anisotropic conductivities on X with Λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">σ1</inf>=Λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">σ2</inf>, then there exists a smooth diffeomorphism <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi :\bar X\rightarrow\bar X$</tex> such that Φ|<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∂X</inf>=Id and Φ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</inf>σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>=σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>.

articleTitle: Bottom of Spectrum of Kähler Manifolds with a Strongly Pseudoconvex Boundary
abstract: We study a class of Kähler manifolds that have a strongly pseudoconvex boundary at infinity. In the Kähler–Einstein case, we formulate a conjecture relating the bottom of spectrum to the CR geometry of the boundary at infinity. Some partial results are obtained.

articleTitle: Hankel Forms and Embedding Theorems in Weighted Dirichlet Spaces
abstract: We show that for a fixed operator-valued analytic function g the boundedness of the bilinear (Hankel-type) form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f,\ h)\rightarrow \int_{\mathbb D}\ {\mathrm tr}(g'^*\ fh')(1-|z|^2)^\alpha\ {\mathrm d}A$</tex>, defined on appropriate cartesian products of dual weighted Dirichlet spaces of Schatten class-valued functions, is equivalent to corresponding Carleson embedding estimates.

articleTitle: Gromov–Witten Invariants of Stable Maps with Fields
abstract: We construct the Gromov–Witten invariants of moduli of stable maps to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^4$</tex> with fields. This is the all genus mathematical theory of the Guffin–Sharpe–Witten model, and is a modified twisted Gromov–Witten invariant of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^4$</tex>. These invariants are constructed using the cosection localization of Kiem–Li, an algebro-geometric analog of Witten’s perturbed equations in Landau–Ginzburg theory. We prove that these invariants coincide, up to sign, with the Gromov–Witten invariants of quintics.

articleTitle: The Distribution of the Number of Points on Trigonal Curves over 𝔽q
abstract: We give a short determination of the distribution of the number of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb F_q$</tex>-rational points on a random trigonal curve over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb F_q$</tex>, in the limit as the genus of the curve goes to infinity. In particular, the expected number of points is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q+2-\frac {1}{q^2+q+1}$</tex>, contrasting with recent analogous results for cyclic p-fold covers of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^1$</tex> and plane curves that have an expected number of points of q+1 (by the work of Kurlberg, Rudnick, Bucur, David, Feigon and Lalín) and curves that are complete intersections that have an expected number of points <q+1 (by work of Bucur and Kedlaya). We also give a conjecture for the expected number of points on a random n-gonal curve with full S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> monodromy based on function field analogs of Bhargava's heuristics for counting number fields.

articleTitle: On the Sup-Norm of Maass Cusp Forms of Large Level: II
abstract: Let f be a Hecke–Maass cuspidal newform of square-free level N and Laplacian eigenvalue λ. It is shown that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$||f||_\infty\ll_{\lambda, \in}\ N^{-1/12+\in} ||f||_2$</tex> for any ϵ>0, with an implied constant depending continuously on λ. The proof is short and self-contained.

We bound the Weyl sum<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\sum_{{\scriptstyle b\ (\mathrm{mod}\ c)} \atop {\scriptstyle b^2 \equiv D\ (\mathrm{mod}\ c)}} e\left({hb \over C}\right)$$</tex>or, more precisely, sums of this sum averaged over the modulus Y <c<2Y and weighted by a nice test function f(c). Employing the theory of automorphic forms, but in a novel fashion, we save a positive power of the range Y even when Y is slightly smaller, by a fixed power, than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sqrt{D}$</tex>. This latter fact is crucial in the applications which are our main concern: to the (weighted) equidistribution of real roots of quadratic equations (Linnik–Skubenko problem), to the asymptotic behavior of cycle integrals of the j-function, and to the representability of all large integers in a suitable residue class as the sum of three squares, one being the square of a prime.

articleTitle: Two Parking Function Bijections: A Sharpening of the q,t-Catalan and Shröder Theorems
abstract: In the following, we give two parking function bijections and describe their relationship to the Frobenius characteristic of the diagonal harmonics. In particular these bijections prove Dyck and Schröder path recursions which combined with certain Hall Littlewood operator recursions proved by Garsia et al. [“Hall–Littlewood operators in the theory of parking functions and diagonal harmonics.” International Mathematics Research Notices (2011)] yield sharper versions of the q,t-Catalan and Shröder Theorems established in Garsia and Haglund [“A proof of the q,t-Catalan positivity conjecture.” Discrete Mathematics 256, no. 3 (2002): 677–717. LaCIM 2000 Conference on Combinatorics, Computer Science and Applications (Montreal, QC)] and Haglund [“A proof of the q,t-Schröder conjecture.” International Mathematics Research Notices no. 11 (2004): 525–60].

articleTitle: Erratum to “Corrections to: Weyl Sums for Quadratic Roots”
A Characterization of the Symmetric Square of a Curve
abstract: We show that the existence on a surface of general type S of irregularity q of an effective divisor D having self-intersection D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>>0 and arithmetic genus q implies that S is birational either to a product of curves or to the second symmetric product of a curve.

articleTitle: The Koszul Complex is the Cotangent Complex
abstract: We extend the Koszul duality theory of associative algebras to algebras over an operad. Recall that in the classical case, this Koszul duality theory relies on an important chain complex: the Koszul complex. We show that the cotangent complex, involved in the cohomology theory of algebras over an operad, plays the role of the Koszul complex.

articleTitle: Lower and Upper Bounds for Nef Cones
abstract: The nef cone of a projective variety Y is an important and often elusive invariant. In this paper, we construct two polyhedral lower bounds and one polyhedral upper bound for the nef cone of Y using an embedding of Y into a toric variety. The lower bounds generalize the combinatorial description of the nef cone of a Mori dream space, while the upper bound generalizes the F-conjecture for the nef cone of the moduli space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar M_{0,n}$</tex> to a wide class of varieties.

articleTitle: Gauge Groups of E0-Semigroups Obtained from Powers Weights
abstract: The gauge group is computed explicitly for a family of E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-semigroups of type II<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> arising from the boundary weight double construction introduced earlier by Jankowski. This family contains many E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-semigroups that are not cocycle conjugate to any examples whose gauge groups have been computed earlier. Further results are obtained regarding the classification up to cocycle conjugacy and up to conjugacy for boundary weight doubles (ϕ,ν) in two separate cases: first in the case when ϕ is unital, invertible and q-pure, and ν is any type II Powers weight, and secondly when ϕ is a unital q-positive map whose range has dimension one and ν(A)=(f,Af) for some function f such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ (1-e^{-x})^{1/2}f(x)\in L^2(0,\ \infty)$</tex>. All E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-semigroups in the former case are cocycle conjugate to the one arising simply from ν, and any two E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-semigroups in the latter case are cocycle conjugate if and only if they are conjugate.

articleTitle: Brownian Motion and Harmonic Functions on Sol(p,q)
abstract: The Lie group Sol(p,q) is the semidirect product induced by the action of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^2$</tex> which is given by (x,y)↦(e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pz</sup>x,e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−qz</sup>y), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z\in\mathbb R$</tex>. Viewing Sol(p,q) as a three-dimensional manifold, it carries a natural Riemannian metric and Laplace–Beltrami operator. We add a linear drift term in the z-variable to the latter, and study the associated Brownian motion with drift. We derive a central limit theorem and compute the rate of escape. Also, we introduce the natural geometric compactification of Sol(p,q) and explain how Brownian motion converges almost surely to the boundary in the resulting topology. We also study all positive harmonic functions for the Laplacian with drift, and determine explicitly all minimal harmonic functions. All these are carried out with a strong emphasis on understanding and using the geometric features of Sol(p,q), and, in particular, the fact that it can be described as the horocyclic product of two hyperbolic planes with curvatures −p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and −q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively.

Let A be a subset of positive relative upper density of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^d$</tex>, the d-tuples of primes. We prove that A contains an affine copy of any set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e\subseteq \mathbb Z^d$</tex>, as long as e is in general position in the sense that the set e∪{0} has at most one point on every coordinate hyperplane.

articleTitle: Invariant Theory and the Heisenberg Vertex Algebra
abstract: The invariant subalgebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal H^+$</tex> of the Heisenberg vertex algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal H$</tex> under its automorphism group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$</tex> was shown by Dong–Nagatomo to be a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal W$</tex>-algebra of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal W(2,4)$</tex>. Similarly, the rank n Heisenberg vertex algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal H(n)$</tex> has the orthogonal group O(n) as its automorphism group, and we conjecture that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal H(n)^{O(n)}$</tex> is a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal W$</tex>-algebra of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal W(2,\ 4,\ 6\ ...,\ n^2+3n)$</tex>. We prove our conjecture for n=2 and n=3, and we show that this conjecture implies that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal H(n)^G$</tex> is strongly finitely generated for any reductive group G⊂O(n).

articleTitle: Weyl–Titchmarsh Theory for Schrödinger Operators with Strongly Singular Potentials
abstract: We develop Weyl–Titchmarsh theory for Schrödinger operators with strongly singular potentials such as perturbed spherical Schrödinger operators (also known as Bessel operators). It is known that in such situations, one can still define a corresponding singular Weyl m-function and it was recently shown that there is also an associated spectral transformation. Here, we will give a general criterion when the singular Weyl function can be analytically extended to the upper half plane. We will derive an integral representation for this singular Weyl function and give a criterion when it is a generalized Nevanlinna function. Moreover, we will show how essential supports for the Lebesgue decomposition of the spectral measure can be obtained from the boundary behavior of the singular Weyl function. Finally, we will prove a local Borg–Marchenko type uniqueness result. Our criteria will in particular cover the aforementioned case of perturbed spherical Schrödinger operators.

articleTitle: On the Maximal Primitive Ideal Corresponding to the Model Nilpotent Orbit
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {g=k}\oplus\mathfrak s$</tex> be a Cartan decomposition of a simple complex Lie algebra corresponding to the Chevalley involution. It is well known that among the set of primitive ideals with the infinitesimal character <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac {1}{2}\rho$</tex>, there is a unique maximal primitive ideal J. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal Q=U(\mathfrak g)/J$</tex>. Let K be a connected compact subgroup with Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak k$</tex> so that the notion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathfrak g, K)$</tex>-modules is well defined. In this paper, we show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal Q^K$</tex> is isomorphic to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U(\mathfrak k)^K$</tex>. In particular, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal Q^K$</tex> is commutative. A consequence of this result is that if W is an irreducible <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathfrak g,K)$</tex>-module annihilated by J, then W is K-multiplicity free and two such irreducible <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathfrak g,K)$</tex>-modules with a common nonzero K-type are isomorphic.

From the view point of noncommutative algebraic geometry (NCAG), a two-sided tilting complex is an analog of a line bundle. In this paper, we define the notion of ampleness for two-sided tilting complexes over finite-dimensional algebras of finite global dimension, and prove its basic properties, which justify the name “ampleness”. From the view point of NCAG, Serre functors are considered to be shifted canonical bundles. A finite-dimensional algebra A of finite global dimension is called Fano if the shifted Serre functor A*[−d] is anti-ample. Some classes of algebras studied before are Fano. We show by examples that the property of A*[−d] from the view point of NCAG captures a representation theoretic property of the algebra A.

articleTitle: On Unconditional Well-Posedness of Modified KdV
abstract: Bourgain [2] proved that the periodic modified Korteweg–de Vries (mKdV) equation is locally well-posed in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^s(\mathbb T), s\geq \frac {1}{2}$</tex>, by introducing new weighted Sobolev spaces X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s,b</sup>, where the uniqueness holds conditionally, namely in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C([0,\ T];\ H^s)\ \cap\ X^{s,\frac {1}{2}}([0,\ T]\ \times\ \mathbb T)$</tex>. In this paper, we establish unconditional well-posedness of mKdV in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C([0,\ T];\ H^s)\ \cap\ X^{s,\frac {1}{2}}([0,\ T]\ \times\ \mathbb T)$</tex>, that is, in addition we establish unconditional uniqueness in C([0,T];H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s\geq \frac {1}{2}$</tex>, of solutions to mKdV. We prove this result via differentiation by parts. For the endpoint case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s\ =\ \frac {1}{2}$</tex>, we perform careful quinti- and septi-linear estimates after the second differentiation by parts.

articleTitle: Petits points des hypersurfaces d’une variété abélienne
abstract: On minore le minimum essentiel des hypersurfaces d’une variété abélienne, en combinant de nouvelles estimations p-adiques et des techniques d’approximation diophantienne. La borne obtenue est optimale “à ε près” en le degré de l’hypersurface. We give a lower bound for the essential minimum of hypersurfaces in an abelian variety, by combining new p-adic estimates and tools from diophantine approximation. This lower bound is optimal “up to an ε” in the degree of the hypersurface.

articleTitle: Gerbal Representations of Double Loop Groups
abstract: A crucial role in representation theory of loop groups of reductive Lie groups and their Lie algebras is played by their nontrivial second cohomology classes, which give rise to their central extensions (the affine Kac–Moody groups and Lie algebras). Loop groups embed into the group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL_\infty$</tex> of continuous automorphisms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb C((t))$</tex>, and these classes come from a second cohomology class of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL_\infty$</tex>. In a similar way, double loop groups embed into a group of automorphisms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb C((t))((s))$</tex>, denoted by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL_{\infty, \infty}$</tex>, which has a nontrivial third cohomology. In this paper, we explain how to realize a third cohomology class in representation theory of a group: it naturally arises when we consider representations on categories rather than vector spaces. We call them “gerbal representations”. We then construct a gerbal representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL_{\infty, \infty}$</tex> (and hence of double loop groups), realizing its nontrivial third cohomology class, on a category of modules over an infinite-dimensional Clifford algebra. This is a two-dimensional analog of the fermionic Fock representations of the ordinary loop groups.

articleTitle: On the Vanishing Ranges for the Cohomology of Finite Groups of Lie Type
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G(\mathbb F_q)$</tex> be a finite Chevalley group defined over the field of q=p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sup> elements, and k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0. A fundamental open and elusive problem has been the computation of the cohomology ring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm H}^\bullet(G(\mathbb F_q)),\ k)$</tex>. In this paper, we determine initial vanishing ranges, which improves upon known results. For root systems of type A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, the first nontrivial cohomology classes are determined when p is larger than the Coxeter number (larger than twice the Coxeter number for type A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> with n>1 and r>1). In the process we make use of techniques involving line bundle cohomology for the flag variety G/B and its relation to combinatorial data from Kostant Partition Functions.

articleTitle: Mirković–Vilonen Polytopes and a Quiver Construction of Crystal Basis in Type A
abstract: In the current paper, we give a quiver theoretical interpretation of Mirković–Vilonen (MV) polytopes in type A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>. As a by-product, we give a new proof of the Anderson–Mirković conjecture that describes the explicit forms of the actions of lowering Kashiwara operators on the set of MV polytopes.

articleTitle: Discrete KdV and Discrete Modified KdV Equations Arising from Motions of Planar Discrete Curves
abstract: We investigate the discrete-time motions of planar discrete curves, and derive discrete integrable equations on a two-dimensional nonuniform lattice. In particular, we obtain the discrete modified KdV equation and the discrete KdV equation, and establish a relationship between them.

articleTitle: Concentration of CMC Surfaces in a 3-manifold
abstract: We prove that simply connected H-surfaces with small diameter in a 3-manifold necessarily concentrate at a critical point of the scalar curvature.

articleTitle: A Note on Discrete Fractional Integral Operators on the Heisenberg Group
abstract: We consider the discrete analog of a fractional integral operator on the Heisenberg group, for which we are able to prove nearly sharp results by means of a simple argument of a combinatorial nature.

articleTitle: Real versus Complex Volumes on Real Algebraic Surfaces
abstract: Let X be a real algebraic surface. The comparison between the volume of D(R) and D(C) for ample divisors D brings us to define the concordance α(X), which is a number between 0 and 1. This number equals 1 when the Picard number ρ(X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf>) is 1, and for some surfaces with a “quite simple” nef cone, for example, Del Pezzo surfaces. For abelian surfaces, α(X) is 1/2 or 1, depending on the existence or not of positive entropy automorphisms on X. In the general case, the existence of such an automorphism gives an upper bound for α(X), namely the ratio of entropies h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">top</inf>(f|X(R))/h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">top</inf>(f|X(C)). Moreover, α(X) is equal to this ratio when the Picard number is 2. An interesting consequence of the inequality is the nondensity of Aut(X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf>) in Diff(X(R)) as soon as α(X)>0. Finally we show, thanks to this upper bound, that there exist K3 surfaces with arbitrary small concordance, considering a deformation of a singular surface of tridegree (2,2,2) in P<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>×P<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>×P<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>.

We classify primitive integer solutions to x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+y<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>=z<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup>. The technique is to combine modular methods at the prime 5, number field enumeration techniques in place of modular methods at the prime 2, Chabauty techniques for elliptic curves over number fields, and local methods.

articleTitle: Classification of Integrable Discrete Equations of Octahedron Type
abstract: We use the consistency approach to classify discrete integrable three-dimensional equations of the octahedron type. They are naturally treated on the root lattice Q(A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) and are consistent on the multi-dimensional lattice Q(A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>). Our list includes the most prominent representatives of this class, the discrete KP equation and its Schwarzian (multi-ratio) version, as well as three further equations. The combinatorics and geometry of the octahedron-type equations are explained. In particular, the consistency on the four-dimensional Delaunay cells has its origin in the classical Desargues theorem of projective geometry. The main technical tool used for the classification is the so-called tripodal form of the octahedron-type equations.

articleTitle: Sums of Kloosterman Sums Over Arithmetic Progressions
abstract: We give an upper bound on the sum of Kloosterman sums S(m,n;c) over an arithmetic progression c≡0(mod q),c≤X with explicit dependence of m,n,q, and X.

articleTitle: The Weil–Petersson Form on an Acyclic Cluster Variety
abstract: For a cluster algebra A, the cluster variety X(A) is the set of maximal ideals in A. Gekhtman, Shapiro, and Vainshtein have defined a 2-form on a dense submanifold of X(A), called the “Weil–Petersson form”. This is a 2-form that encodes much of the combinatorial information of the cluster algebra. We explore the question of when this form extends to the entire cluster variety (as a Kähler 2-form). In particular, we show that, for acyclic cluster varieties, the Weil–Petersson 2-form extends to a regular Kähler 2-form on the entire cluster variety. If this cluster variety is smooth, then the Weil–Petersson form extends as a differential 2-form everywhere.

articleTitle: The Isoperimetric Inequality and Quasiconformal Maps on Manifolds with Finite Total Q-curvature
abstract: In this paper, we obtain the isoperimetric inequality on a conformally flat manifold with finite total Q-curvature. This is a higher dimensional analog of Li and Tam’s result [“Complete surfaces with finite total curvature.” Journal of Differential Geometry 33 (1991): 139–68] on surfaces with finite total Gaussian curvature. The main step in the proof is based on the construction of a quasiconformal map the Jacobian of which is suitably bounded.

articleTitle: Bennequin Type Inequalities in Lens Spaces
abstract: We give criteria for an invariant of lens space links to bound the maximal self-linking number in certain tight contact lens spaces. Our result generalizes that given by Ng [“A Skein approach to Bennequin type inequalities.” International Mathematics Research Notices 2008, no. 24 (2008): 18] for links in S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> with the standard tight contact structure. As a corollary we extend the Franks–Williams–Morton inequality to the setting of lens spaces.

articleTitle: The Corona Factorization Property, Stability, and the Cuntz Semigroup of a C*-algebra
abstract: The Corona Factorization Property, originally invented to study extensions of C*-algebras, conveys essential information about the intrinsic structure of the C*-algebra. We show that the Corona Factorization Property of a σ-unital C*-algebra is completely captured by its Cuntz semigroup (of equivalence classes of positive elements in the stabilization of A). The corresponding condition in the Cuntz semigroup is a very weak comparability property termed the Corona Factorization Property for semigroups. Using this result, one can, for example, show that all unital C*-algebras with a finite decomposition rank have the Corona Factorization Property. Applying similar techniques, we study the related question of when C*-algebras are stable. We give an intrinsic characterization, that we term property (S), of C*-algebras that have no nonzero unital quotients and no nonzero bounded 2-quasitraces. We then show that property (S) is equivalent to stability provided that the Cuntz semigroup of the C*-algebra has another (also very weak) comparability property, that we call the ω-comparison property.

articleTitle: Uniqueness and Nonuniqueness for Ricci Flow on Surfaces: Reverse Cusp Singularities
abstract: We extend the notion of what it means for a complete Ricci flow to have a given initial metric, and consider the resulting well-posedness issues that arise in the two-dimensional case. On one hand, we construct examples of nonuniqueness by showing that surfaces with cusps can evolve either by keeping the cusps or by contracting them. On the other hand, by adding a noncollapsedness assumption for the initial metric, we establish a uniqueness result.

articleTitle: An Improved Sum–Product Inequality in Fields of Prime Order
abstract: This note proves the sum–product inequality <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$${\mathrm max}(|A\cdot A|,\ |A+A|)\gg|A|^{1+\frac {1}{11}}\frac {1}{{\mathrm log}^{\frac {4}{11}}|A|},$$</tex> for sets of cardinality <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1<|A|<\sqrt{p}$</tex> in prime fields <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb F_p$</tex>.

articleTitle: Cesàro Convergence of Spherical Averages for Measure-Preserving Actions of Markov Semigroups and Groups
abstract: Cesàro convergence of spherical averages is proved for measure-preserving actions of Markov semigroups and groups. Convergence in the mean is established for functions in L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\leq p<\infty$</tex>, and pointwise convergence for functions in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^{\infty}$</tex>. In particular, for measure-preserving actions of word hyperbolic groups (in the sense of Gromov) we obtain Cesàro convergence of spherical averages with respect to any symmetric set of generators.

articleTitle: The Dimension of Weakly Mean Porous Measures: a Probabilistic Approach
abstract: Using probabilistic ideas, we prove that if μ is a mean porous measure on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^{n}$</tex>, then the packing dimension of μ is strictly smaller than n. Moreover, we give an explicit bound for the packing dimension, which is asymptotically sharp in the case of small porosity. This result was stated in [D. B. Beliaev and S. K. Smirnov, “On dimension of porous measures”, Mathematische Annalen 323 (2002): 123–41], but the proof given there is not correct. We also give estimates on the dimension of weakly mean porous measures, which improve another result of Beliaev and Smirnov.

articleTitle: Geometric Renormalization Below the Ground State
abstract: The caloric gauge was introduced in [38] by Tao with studying large data energy-critical wave maps mapping from R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+1</sup> to hyperbolic space H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup> in view. In [1] Bejenaru et al. adapted the caloric gauge to the setting of Schrödinger maps from R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d+1</sup> to the standard sphere S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>↪R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> with initial data small in the critical Sobolev norm. Here we develop the caloric gauge in a bounded geometry setting with a construction valid up to the ground-state energy, which for maps <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2+1}\rightarrow \mathcal M^m$</tex> is the natural limitation imposed by the harmonic map heat flow used to define the caloric gauge. In [34] we apply these results to the study of Schrödinger maps lying below the ground-state energy.

articleTitle: On q, t-characters and the l-weight Jordan Filtration of Standard Uq(Ŝl2)-modules
abstract: The Cartan subalgebra of the quantum loop algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_{q}({\mathrm L}\mathfrak {sl}_2)$</tex> is generated by a family of mutually commuting operators, responsible for the l-weight decomposition of finite-dimensional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_{q}({\mathrm L}\mathfrak {sl}_2)$</tex>-modules. The natural Jordan filtration induced by these operators is generically non-trivial on l-weight spaces of dimension greater than 1. We derive, for every standard module of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_{q}({\mathrm L}\mathfrak {sl}_2)$</tex>, the dimensions of the Jordan grades and prove that they can be directly read off from the t-dependence of the q,t-characters introduced by Nakajima. To do so, we construct explicit bases for the standard modules of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_{q}({\mathrm L}\mathfrak {sl}_2)$</tex> with respect to which the Cartan generators are upper-triangular. The basis vectors of each l-weight space are labeled by the elements of a ranked poset from the family L(m,n).

articleTitle: The Galois Module Structure of ℓ-adic Realizations of Picard 1-motives and Applications
abstract: Let Z→Z′ be a finite G-Galois cover of smooth, projective curves over an arbitrary algebraically closed field κ, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal S$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal T$</tex> be G-equivariant, disjoint, finite, non-empty sets of closed points on Z, such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal S$</tex> contains the ramification locus of the cover. In this context, we prove that the ℓ-adic realizations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_\ell (\mathcal M_{\mathcal S,\mathcal T})$</tex> of the Picard 1-motive <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{\mathcal S,\mathcal T}$</tex> associated to the data <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(Z,\kappa,\mathcal S,\mathcal T)$</tex> are G-cohomologically trivial and therefore <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb Z_\ell [G]$</tex>-projective modules of finite rank, for all prime numbers ℓ. In the process, we give a new proof of Nakajima’s theorem [Equivariant form of the Deuring–Safarevic formula for Hasse–Witt invariants. Mathematische Zeitschrift 190, no. 4 (1985): 559–66] on the Galois module structure of the semi-simple piece <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega_Z(-[\mathcal S])^{s}$</tex> under the action of the Cartier operator on a certain space of differentials <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega_Z(-[\mathcal S])$</tex> associated to Z and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal S$</tex>, assuming that char(κ)=p. As a main arithmetic application of these results, we consider the situation where the set of data <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(Z,\ Z',\ \mathcal S,\ \mathcal T)$</tex> is defined over a finite field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb F_{q}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\kappa:+\bar {\mathbb F}_{q}$</tex>. We combine results of Deligne and Tate, Berthelot, Bloch and Illusie with our cohomological triviality result to prove that in this context we have an equality of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb Z_\ell\left[\left[\bar G\right]\right]$</tex>-ideals <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Theta_\mathcal {S,T}(\gamma^{-1}))={\mathrm Fit}_{\mathbb Z_\ell\left[\left[\bar G\right]\right]}(T_\ell(M_{\mathcal {S,T}}))$</tex>, for all prime numbers ℓ, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar G:=G\ \times\ {\mathrm Gal}(\bar {\mathbb F}_q/\mathbb F_q),\ \gamma$</tex> is the q-power arithmetic Frobenius morphism (viewed as a distinguished topological generator of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm Gal}(\bar {\mathbb F}_q/\mathbb F_q)$</tex>) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Theta _{\mathcal {S,T}}(u)\in\mathbb Z[G][u]$</tex> is the (polynomial) G-equivariant L-function associated to the data <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(Z,\ Z',\ \mathbb F_{q},\ \mathcal {S,\ T})$</tex>. We obtain this way a Galois-equivariant refinement of results of Deligne and Tate [Les conjectures de Stark sur les fonctions L d’Artin en s=0. Progress in Mathematics 47. Boston, MA: Birkhauser Boston Inc., 1984. Lecture notes edited by Dominique Bernardi and Norbert Schappacher.] on ℓ-adic realizations of Picard 1-motives associated to (global) function fields. As an immediate application, we prove refinements of the classical Brumer-Stark and Coates-Sinnott conjectures linking special values of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Theta_\mathcal {S,T}(u)$</tex> to certain invariants of ideal-class groups and étale cohomology groups, respectively. In our upcoming work, we will show how several other classical conjectures on special values of global L-functions follow from the results obtained in this paper.

This article gives an analog of Taylor’s trick in the context of motives for absolute Hodge cycles. The aforementioned trick, first sketched by Taylor in a letter to Clozel, gives two conditions ensuring that an mn-dimensional ℓ-adic Galois representation is divisible by m. We give a detailed proof of this result, and extend it to motives by using Tannakian duality.

articleTitle: The Rational Cohomology of the Mapping Class Group Vanishes in its Virtual Cohomological Dimension
abstract: Let Mod<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> be the mapping class group of a genus g≥2 surface. The group Mod<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> has virtual cohomological dimension 4g−5. In this note, we use a theorem of Broaddus and the combinatorics of chord diagrams to prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^{4g-5}({\mathrm Mod}_g;\ \mathbb Q)=0$</tex>.

articleTitle: Distribution of Elements of Cosets of Small Subgroups and Applications
abstract: We obtain a series of estimates on the number of small integers and small order Farey fractions that belong to a given coset of a subgroup of order t of the group of units of the residue ring modulo a prime p, in the case when t is small compared to p. We give two applications of these results: to the simultaneous distribution of two high-degree monomials x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k1</sup> and x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k2</sup> modulo p and to a question of Holden and Moree on fixed points of the discrete logarithm.

We algebraically prove K-stability of polarized Calabi–Yau varieties and canonically polarized varieties with mild singularities. In particular, the “stable varieties” introduced by Kollár–Shepherd-Barron [“Threefolds and deformation of surface singularities.” Inventiones Mathematicae 91 (1988): 299–338] and Alexeev [“Moduli spaces M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g,n</inf>(W) for surfaces.” Proceeding of “Higher-dimensional complex varieties (Trento, 1994)”, de Gruyter, Berlin, 1996, 1–22], which form compact moduli space, are proven to be K-stable although it is well known that they are not necessarily asymptotically (semi) stable. As a consequence, we have orbifold counterexamples to the folklore conjecture “K-stability implies asymptotic stability”. They have Kähler–Einstein (orbifold) metrics, so the result of Donaldson [“Scalar curvature and projective embeddings. I.” Journal of Differential Geometry 59, no. 3 (2001): 479–522] does not hold for orbifolds.

articleTitle: A Borg–Levinson Theorem for Higher Order Elliptic Operators
abstract: We establish the Borg–Levinson theorem for elliptic operators of higher order with constant coefficients. The case of incomplete spectral data is also considered.

The main goal of this paper is to give a bound on the denominators of Igusa class polynomials for genus 2 curves. Our motivation is from cryptography via the use of genus 2 curves with a prescribed number of points, and from class invariants with a view towards class field theory and Stark’s conjectures. All known methods for constructing such curves rely on complex multiplication and the calculation of Igusa class polynomials. These polynomials have rational coefficients and their determination requires extensive computation and precision. The results of this paper make it possible now to perform complexity analysis of these algorithms. The analysis for bounding the denominators also informs the prime factorization for certain class invariants. Both problems are translated into questions about isomorphisms between principally polarized abelian surfaces with complex multiplication and products of elliptic curves with the product polarization, over local artinian rings. We give an overview of Igusa’s results on the moduli space of genus 2 curves and the method to construct genus 2 curves via their Igusa invariants. We also give a complete characterization of the reduction type of a CM abelian surface, for any type of prime decomposition of the prime, including ramified primes. The methods used in the proofs of the main results involve studying the embedding problem of the quartic CM field into certain matrix algebras over quaternions and invoking techniques from crystalline deformation theory.

The Levi geometry at weakly pseudoconvex boundary points of domains in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb C^n,\ n\geq3$</tex>, is sufficiently complicated that there are no universal model domains with which to compare a general domain. Good models may be constructed by bumping outward a pseudoconvex, finite-type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega \subset \mathbb C^3$</tex> in such a way that: (i) pseudoconvexity is preserved, (ii) the (locally) larger domain has a simpler defining function, and (iii) the lowest possible orders of contact of the bumped domain with ∂Ω, at the site of the bumping, are realized. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega \subset \mathbb C^n, n\geq3$</tex>, it is, in general, hard to meet the last two requirements. Such well-controlled bumping is possible when Ω is h-extendible/semiregular. We examine a family of domains in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb C^3$</tex> that is strictly larger than the family of h-extendible/semiregular domains and construct explicit models for these domains by bumping.

articleTitle: On Quadratic Distinction of Automorphic Sheaves
abstract: We prove a geometric version of a classical result on the characterization of an irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm GL}_n(\mathbb A_E)$</tex> being the base change of a stable cuspidal representation of the quasi-split unitary group associated to the quadratic extension E/F, via the nonvanishing of certain period integrals, called being distinguished. We show that certain cohomology of an automorphic sheaf of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n,X</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">′</sup> is nonvanishing if and only if the corresponding local system E on X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">′</sup> is conjugate self-dual with respect to an étale double cover X′/X of curves, which directly relates to the base change from the associated unitary group. In particular, the geometric setting makes sense over any base field.

articleTitle: Surjectivity of the Comparison Map in Bounded Cohomology for Hermitian Lie Groups
abstract: We investigate the implications of Gromov’s theorem on boundedness of primary characteristic classes for the continuous bounded cohomology of a semisimple Lie group G. We deduce that the comparison map from continuous bounded cohomology to continuous cohomology is surjective for a large class of semisimple Lie groups, including all Hermitian groups. Our proof is based on a geometric implementation of the canonical map from the cohomology of the classifying space of G to the continuous group cohomology of G. We obtain this implementation by establishing a variant of Kobayashi–Ono–Hirzebruch duality.

articleTitle: Do Uniruled Six-manifolds Contain Sol Lagrangian Submanifolds?
abstract: We prove using symplectic field theory combined with some Gromov–Witten theory that if the suspension of a hyperbolic diffeomorphism of the two-torus Lagrangian embeds in a closed uniruled symplectic six-manifold, then its first rational homology is generated by the boundary of a symplectic disk. This prevents any Sol manifold from being in the real locus of an orientable real Del Pezzo fibration over a curve, confirming an expectation of Kollár. It also constrains Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of uniruled symplectic four-manifolds.

Brundan, Kleshchev, and Wang have introduced a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb Z$</tex>-grading on the Specht modules of the degenerate and nondegenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebras of type G(ℓ,1,n). In this paper, we show that the induced Specht modules have an explicit filtration by shifts of graded Specht modules. This proves a conjecture of Brundan, Kleshchev, and Wang. To prove these results, we first establish several strong results about the transition matrices between the seminormal, standard, and homogeneous bases of these algebras and similar results for the action of the Jucys–Murphy elements on these bases.

articleTitle: Centro-Affine Invariants for Smooth Convex Bodies
abstract: Employing a centro-affine flow on smooth convex bodies, we generate new equicentro-affine differential invariants. One class of the newly defined invariants is the object of a sharp isoperimetric inequality, while other new inequalities on known equicentro-affine invariants are obtained as a byproduct of the flow’s study. Furthermore, this approach led to a geometric interpretation of the L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ϕ</inf> affine surface area recently introduced by Ludwig and Reitzner.

articleTitle: Solving the Sixth Painlevé Equation: Towards the Classification of all the Critical Behaviors and the Connection Formulae
abstract: The critical behavior of a three real parameter class of solutions of the sixth Painlevé equation is computed, and parametrized in terms of monodromy data of the associated 2×2 matrix linear Fuchsian system of ODE. The class may contain solutions with poles accumulating at the critical point. The study of this class closes a gap in the description of the transcendents in an one to one correspondence with the monodromy data. These transcendents are reviewed in the paper. Some formulas that relate the monodromy data to the critical behaviors of the four real (two complex) parameter class of solutions are missing in the literature, so they are computed here. A computational procedure to write the full expansion of the four and three real parameter class of solutions is proposed.

articleTitle: The Sine Transform of Isotropic Measures
abstract: Sharp isoperimetric inequalities for the sine transform of even isotropic measures are established. The corresponding reverse inequalities are obtained in an asymptotically optimal form. These new inequalities have direct applications to strong volume estimates for convex bodies from data about their sections or projections.

articleTitle: Lower Bounds on Odd Order Character Sums
abstract: A classical result of Paley shows that there are infinitely many quadratic characters χ(mod q) whose character sums get as large as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sqrt{q}\ {\log \log}\ q$</tex>; this implies that a conditional upper bound of Montgomery and Vaughan cannot be improved. In this paper, we derive analogous lower bounds on character sums for characters of odd order, which are best possible in view of the corresponding conditional upper bounds recently obtained by the first author.

articleTitle: Uniqueness of Normalized Homeomorphic Solutions to Nonlinear Beltrami Equations
abstract: We settle the problem of the uniqueness of normalized homeomorphic solutions to the nonlinear Beltrami equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar {\partial }\ f(z)=\mathcal H(z,\ \partial f(z))$</tex>. It turns out that the uniqueness holds under explicit bounds on the ellipticity constant of the equation at infinity, but not in general.

articleTitle: A Note on Brill–Noether Theory and Rank-Determining Sets for Metric Graphs
abstract: We produce open subsets of the moduli space of metric graphs without separating edges where the dimensions of Brill–Noether loci are larger than the corresponding Brill–Noether numbers. These graphs also have minimal rank-determining sets that are larger than expected, giving counterexamples to a conjecture of Luo. Furthermore, limits of these graphs have Brill–Noether loci of the expected dimension, so dimensions of Brill–Noether loci of metric graphs do not vary upper semicontinuously in families. Motivated by these examples, we study a notion of rank for the Brill–Noether locus of a metric graph, closely analogous to the Baker–Norine definition of the rank of a divisor. We show that ranks of Brill–Noether loci vary upper semicontinuously in families of metric graphs and are related to dimensions of Brill–Noether loci of algebraic curves by a specialization inequality.

articleTitle: The Transition between the Gap Probabilities from the Pearcey to the Airy Process—a Riemann–Hilbert Approach
abstract: We consider the gap probability for the Pearcey and Airy processes; we set up a Riemann–Hilbert approach (different from the standard one) whereby the asymptotic analysis for large gap/large time of the Pearcey process is shown to factorize into two independent Airy processes using the Deift–Zhou steepest descent analysis. Additionally, we relate the theory of Fredholm determinants of integrable kernels and the theory of isomonodromic tau function. Using the Riemann–Hilbert problem mentioned above, we construct a suitable Lax pair formalism for the Pearcey gap probability and re-derive the two nonlinear PDEs recently found and additionally find a third one not reducible to those.

articleTitle: Twisted K-Homology and Group-Valued Moment Maps
abstract: Let G be a compact, simply connected Lie group. We develop a ‘quantization functor’ from prequantized quasi-Hamiltonian G-spaces (M,ω,Φ) at level k to the fusion ring (Verlinde algebra) R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>(G). The quantization <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal Q(M)\in R_k(G)$</tex> is defined as a push-forward in twisted equivariant K-homology. It may be computed by a fixed point formula, similar to the equivariant index theorem for Spin<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>-Dirac operators. Using the formula, we calculate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal Q(M)$</tex> in several examples.

articleTitle: Descent and Forms of Tensor Categories
abstract: We develop a theory of descent and forms of tensor categories over arbitrary fields. We describe the general scheme of classification of such forms using algebraic and homotopical language, and give examples of explicit classification of forms. We also discuss the problem of categorification of weak fusion rings, and for the simplest families of such rings, determine which ones are categorifiable.

articleTitle: Sharp Asymptotics for Toeplitz Determinants and Convergence Towards the Gaussian Free Field on Riemann Surfaces
abstract: We consider canonical determinantal random point processes with N particles on a compact Riemann surface X defined with respect to the constant curvature metric. We establish strong exponential concentration of measure type properties involving Dirichlet norms of linear statistics. This gives an optimal central limit theorem (CLT), saying that the fluctuations of the corresponding empirical measures converge, in the large N limit, towards the Laplacian of the Gaussian free field on X in the strongest possible sense. The CLT is also shown to be equivalent to a new sharp strong Szegö-type theorem for Toeplitz determinants in this context. One of the ingredients in the proofs are new Bergman kernel asymptotics providing exponentially small error terms in a constant curvature setting.

We prove a simple explicit formula for the local Katz–Radon transform of an ℓ-adic representation of the Galois group of the fraction field of a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring with positive residual characteristic, which can be defined as the local additive convolution with a fixed tame character. The formula is similar to the one proved by Arinkin in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal D$</tex>-module setting, and answers a question posed by Katz.

articleTitle: One-Skeleton Galleries, the Path Model, and a Generalization of Macdonald’s Formula for Hall–Littlewood Polynomials
abstract: We give a direct geometric interpretation of the path model using galleries in the 1-skeleton of the Bruhat–Tits building associated with a semi-simple algebraic group. This interpretation allows us to compute the coefficients of the expansion of the Hall–Littlewood polynomials in the monomial basis. The formula we obtain is a “geometric compression” of the one proved by Schwer, its specialization to the case A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> turns out to be equivalent to Macdonald’s formula.

articleTitle: Matrix-Valued Orthogonal Polynomials Related to (SU(2)×SU(2), diag)
abstract: The matrix-valued spherical functions for the pair (K×K,K), K=SU(2), are studied. By restriction to the subgroup A, the matrix-valued spherical functions are diagonal. For suitable set of spherical functions, we take these diagonals as a matrix-valued function, which are the full spherical functions. Their orthogonality is a consequence of the Schur orthogonality relations. From the full spherical functions, we obtain matrix-valued orthogonal polynomials of arbitrary size, and they satisfy a three-term recurrence relation which follows by considering tensor product decompositions. An explicit expression for the weight and the complete block-diagonalization of the matrix-valued orthogonal polynomials is obtained. From the explicit expression, we obtain right-hand-sided differential operators of first and second order for which the matrix-valued orthogonal polynomials are eigenfunctions. We study the low-dimensional cases explicitly, and for these cases additional results, such as the Rodrigues’ formula and being eigenfunctions to first-order differential–difference and second-order differential operators, are obtained.

articleTitle: Autoequivalences of the Tensor Category of Uq𝔤-modules
abstract: We prove that for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q\in \mathbb C^*$</tex> not a nontrivial root of unity the cohomology group defined by invariant 2-cocycles in a completion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_q\mathfrak g$</tex> is isomorphic to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^2(P/Q;\mathbb T)$</tex>, where P and Q are the weight and root lattices of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$mathfrak g$</tex>, respectively. This implies that the group of autoequivalences of the tensor category of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_q\mathfrak g$</tex>-modules is the semidirect product of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^2(P/Q;\mathbb T)$</tex> and the automorphism group of the based root datum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$mathfrak g$</tex>. For q=1 we also obtain similar results for all compact connected separable groups.

We give a new upper bound for the generation time of a tilting object and use it to verify, in some new cases, a conjecture of Orlov on the Rouquier dimension of the derived category of coherent sheaves on a smooth variety.

articleTitle: An Effective Schmidt’s Subspace Theorem for Projective Varieties Over Function Fields
abstract: We deduce an effective version of Schmidt’s subspace theorem on a smooth projective variety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal X \subset \mathbb P^{N}$</tex> over a function field of characteristic zero for divisors of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal X$</tex> coming from hypersurfaces in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^{N}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Loci of Integrability, Zero Loci, and Stability Under Integration for Constructible Functions on Euclidean Space with Lebesgue Measure
abstract: We introduce and study loci of integrability.
